messages:
sam: heads up — our CI started failing for the edge runtime tests only. Error: 'Unexpected token ‘export’' coming from src/runtime/kv.ts which we mock. Locally the same commit sometimes passes. Anyone seen this flake?

laura: runner? jest or vitest in CI?

sam: CI runs jest 29 (legacy config), many devs run vitest locally. package.json has "type": "module" and we publish dual cjs/mjs entry points via exports. tests are .ts.

aj: Mixed runners + ESM = usual footgun. For Jest + ESM you need a couple things: set tsconfig to { module: 'nodenext', moduleResolution: 'nodenext' }, add `extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts']`, and use a transform like `esbuild-jest`. Without that Jest will treat files as CJS and choke on `export`.

mika: Also check node version. CI image uses node 18.10 while most devs are on 18.16 — module loader differences can make mocks fail intermittently. Pin node in CI or use the same runner.

sam: Our test does `jest.resetModules()` then `const kv = require('../runtime/kv')` which I now suspect is the culprit. We mock the module earlier.

laura: yep, require() will break for ESM. With jest you need to use the unstable ESM mock APIs and dynamic import after mocking. Example that fixed a similar bug for us:

// test file (Node 18+, Jest 29+)
await jest.unstable_mockModule('../runtime/kv', () => ({ default: mockKV, get: () => mockGet }));
const { default: kv } = await import('../runtime/kv');

aj: important: don't import the module (even indirectly) before calling unstable_mockModule. Any top-level import will lock module resolution to the real implementation.

mika: Another flake source: some deps in node_modules are ESM-only and get skipped by transformIgnorePatterns. If CI picks a different lockfile or node image, you may hit untransformed ESM in node_modules -> throw syntax errors. Add those packages to transform or relax transformIgnorePatterns.

sam: Would moving tests to vitest be simpler? Vitest + Vite auto handle ESM + TS and vi.mock works more predictably for edge-like code.

laura: That's tempting but we still have a large Jest surface (some infra tests rely on jest snapshots). For a quick fix we'll try: 1) pin node in CI, 2) add esbuild-jest transform + extensionsToTreatAsEsm, 3) replace require() usage with dynamic import + unstable_mockModule. If flakes persist, consider a smaller Vitest migration for edge tests.

devex-bot: CI: build/edge-tests #997 failed  https://ci.internal/builds/997  failing tests: sdk/edge/kv.spec.ts :disappointed:

sam: I'll open a PR with the esbuild-jest config + node 18.16 image and convert one failing test to the unstable_mockModule pattern to validate. If that stabilizes CI we can roll out changes.

laura: thanks — please tag me on the PR. If it still flakes I'll paste full stack and we can triage deeper. :pray:
